tip: Rekha is the subject, so 'her' homework is अपना (apna), not उसका (uska) – उसका would mean someone ELSE's homework, not her own.
अपनी माँ (apni maa) – अपना (apna) matches the thing owned, not the owner: माँ (maa) is feminine, so it's अपनी whether Lakshmi or her brother writes.
In commands 'your' is अपना too: अपना पूरा नाम बताइए (apna poora naam bataiye) = tell your full name – the doer is 'you', so अपना points back at you.
अपना खाना ख़ुद बनाया (apna khaana khud banaya) – two self-words: अपना = his own (the food), ख़ुद = himself (did the cooking).
अपने आप (apne aap) = by oneself: Kavita finished सारा काम (saara kaam = all the work) with no help. For things, the same phrase means 'on its own'.
अपनी-अपनी जगह (apni-apni jagah) – doubling अपना spreads it over everyone: each to their OWN place. Hindi repeats a word to mean each/respective.
आपका अपना घर (aapka apna ghar) – अपना stacked after आपका means 'your very own'. A warm host formula: this house is yours too, not just ours.
ख़ुदा हाफ़िज़ (khuda haafiz) – literally 'God (is your) protector', a goodbye from Urdu, common in everyday Hindi alongside नमस्ते (namaste).
मनवा ही ली (manva hi li) – मानना (maanna = accept) plus -वा means getting OTHERS to accept: Vikas didn't just state अपनी बात (apni baat = his point), he made them agree.
You don't miss things in Hindi – the memory comes to you: मुझे (mujhe = to me) + याद आती है (yaad aati hai = memory comes) = I miss my country.
